title: Color Sorting Basket
description: Sort colored balls into matching baskets to build visual discrimination and classification skills.
materialsNeeded: Colored plastic balls or toys, colored bins or baskets
benefits: Improves color recognition, categorization, and fine motor grasp coordination.
instructions: Place colored baskets in front of the child. Hand them a ball, name the color clearly, and guide them to place it into the matching basket. Cheer for every successful match!

title: Mirror Me - Action Imitation
description: Parent performs simple facial and motor actions while child imitates, building social engagement.
benefits: Builds imitation skills, eye contact, reciprocal social interaction, and joint attention.
instructions: Sit facing your child at eye level. Clap your hands and say 'Mirror me! Clap!'. Wait for them to copy. Progress to funny faces, touching your nose, or waving.

title: Sound Match Cards
description: Match animal sound recordings to picture cards to build auditory-visual association.
materialsNeeded: Animal picture cards, smartphone or tablet with animal sounds
benefits: Improves auditory processing, receptive language, and focus.
instructions: Play a 3-second animal sound (like a cow or lion). Ask the child: 'Who makes this sound?' Encourage them to point to or pick up the matching animal flashcard.

title: Sensory Bin Exploration
description: Tactile play in a rice or bean bin with hidden toys to develop tactile regulation.
materialsNeeded: Plastic tub, dry rice or beans, small hidden figures, scoops and spoons
benefits: Desensitizes tactile defensiveness, calms the nervous system, and strengthens finger grasp.
instructions: Fill a shallow plastic tub with colored rice or dried beans. Bury 5 small animal toys. Guide the child to dig in and discover the treasures one by one.

title: Feelings Flashcards & Emotion Gestures
description: Explore facial expression cards together to label and understand daily emotions.
materialsNeeded: Emotion flashcards (Happy, Sad, Angry, Surprised, Calm)
benefits: Expands expressive emotional vocabulary, self-regulation, and empathetic understanding.
instructions: Show a card showing a smiling child. Say 'Happy! I feel happy when we play.' Ask the child to make a happy face with you in a mirror.

title: Visual Memory Flip Game
description: Flip paired tiles to find identical symbols and improve short-term visual recall.
materialsNeeded: 6 to 12 paired cards (fruits, vehicles, or animals)
benefits: Builds active working memory, concentration, and patience in turn-taking.
instructions: Lay 6 pairs of cards face down on a table. Take turns flipping two cards. If they match, keep them; if not, flip them back over and remember their positions.

title: Geometric Shape Puzzle Board
description: Manipulate wooden geometric shapes into corresponding cutouts on a puzzle board.
materialsNeeded: Wooden shape puzzle (circle, square, triangle, star)
benefits: Develops spatial reasoning, pincer grasp, and bilateral hand coordination.
instructions: Empty the shape pieces and place them beside the board. Model rotating a piece to fit into the corresponding groove, then support your child's hands to try.

title: Bubble Pop & Verbal Cues
description: Blow soap bubbles and use verbal prompts like 'Ready, Set, POP!' to encourage vocalization.
benefits: Motivates vocal sound initiation, breath control, and joint gaze tracking.
instructions: Dip the wand and hold it near your mouth. Pause and wait for eye contact or a sound. Say 'Ready, Set...' and let the child prompt 'Go!'. Blow bubbles and pop them together shouting 'POP!'.

title: Sensory Finger Paint Expression
description: Non-toxic finger painting on textured paper to express feelings through colors and tactile art.
materialsNeeded: Washable kid-safe finger paints, large paper sheets, apron
benefits: Sensory regulation, self-expression, creative freedom, and tactile stimulation.
instructions: Tape large white card stock to a table. Spoon out small dollops of paint. Allow the child to use fingers, palms, or sponge stamps freely without pressure for a specific result.

title: Indoor Pillow Obstacle Course
description: Crawl over cushions, step between tape lines, and crawl through tunnels for gross motor planning.
materialsNeeded: Sofa cushions, pillows, painter tape on floor, collapsible play tunnel
benefits: Proprioceptive input, vestibular balance, core muscle strength, and motor planning.
instructions: Set a safe sequence in the living room: step across 3 pillows, balance along a tape line, then crawl through the tunnel to ring a bell at the finish line.

title: Nature Texture Scavenger Hunt
description: Walk outdoors collecting rough bark, smooth pebbles, green leaves, and soft petals.
materialsNeeded: Egg carton or small basket, checklist with pictures of nature items
benefits: Grounding in nature, outdoor sensory integration, descriptive language, and physical activity.
instructions: Take a walk in a garden or park with an egg carton. Guide the child to touch different textures and collect one piece for each carton compartment.

title: First-Then Visual Routine Board
description: Structure morning and evening routines with a high-contrast visual sequencing chart.
materialsNeeded: Velcro strip, picture icons (Brush teeth, Wear shoes, Eat breakfast)
benefits: Reduces transition anxiety, builds independent daily routine habits, and reinforces structure.
instructions: Attach 'First' task icon and 'Then' reward/next task icon. Guide child to move completed card to the 'Done' box with cheerful verbal reinforcement.
